title: White House AI Evaluation Framework Completed on Time but Kept Confidential, OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google Didn't See the Full Text
excerpt: According to Axios, the U.S. government announced on Monday local time that it had completed a voluntary assessment framework for advanced AI models on schedule
content_html:
According to Axios, the U.S. government announced on Monday local time that it had completed a voluntary assessment framework for advanced AI models on schedule. However, the White House has not revealed the specific content of the framework, nor has it specified which agencies or companies have reviewed the document, and it has also not provided a timeline for when companies will begin adopting it.

This framework originated from a presidential executive order signed on June 2, aiming to provide AI developers with a structured process to help them collaborate with the government in determining whether models under development fall within regulatory scope. The framework should clarify the confidentiality requirements, cybersecurity requirements, internal risk management requirements, intellectual property protection, and non-disclosure provisions that the government must follow when obtaining relevant models up to 30 days before their release. It should also define which "trusted partners" can gain early access to the model.

What should be public remains hidden, and what should be confidential is even more so.

Notably, the executive order explicitly classified the benchmark testing process for evaluating an AI model's advanced cyberattack capabilities as confidential, and the threshold parameters for applicable models are also considered confidential information, disclosed only to AI developers and researchers "under appropriate circumstances." However, the voluntary framework itself was not classified as confidential, so policymakers and observers had previously expected to see the details—yet the White House has still not made them public.

A White House official's response was rather telling: "Even if certain information is not classified, it does not mean we will disseminate it to everyone." He also stated that the government is engaging with "more than just Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google" in terms of industry partners. By the deadline, these three AI labs had already provided feedback on the framework draft to the government.

AI companies are eager to obtain clear guidance as soon as possible to determine whether their models under development may be subject to the framework. According to informed sources, the White House plans to hold staff-level meetings with relevant companies on Tuesday local time to review the framework. When the world's most powerful AI models will face what kind of regulatory rules, even the companies that provided feedback remain in the dark, and this "completed but not visible" framework itself may already reveal a lot.

content_html_zh:
据Axios报道，美国政府当地时间周一宣布，已按期完成先进人工智能模型的自愿评估框架。 不过，白宫并未透露该框架的具体内容，也没有具体说明哪些机构或公司审查了该文件，也没有提供企业何时开始采用该文件的时间表。

该框架源于6月2日签署的总统行政命令，旨在为人工智能开发者提供结构化流程，帮助他们与政府合作确定正在开发的模型是否属于监管范围。 该框架应明确政府在发布前 30 天内获取相关模型时必须遵守的保密要求、网络安全要求、内部风险管理要求、知识产权保护和保密规定。 它还应该定义哪些“值得信赖的合作伙伴”可以尽早访问该模型。

该公开的事情却被隐瞒了，该保密的事情更是如此。

值得注意的是，该行政命令明确将评估人工智能模型高级网络攻击能力的基准测试过程列为机密，适用模型的阈值参数也被视为机密信息，仅在“适当情况下”向人工智能开发人员和研究人员披露。 然而，自愿框架本身并未被列为机密，因此政策制定者和观察人士此前预计会看到细节，但白宫仍未将其公开。

一位白宫官员的回应相当有说服力：“即使某些信息不是机密，也不意味着我们会将其传播给所有人。” 他还表示，就行业合作伙伴而言，政府正在与“不仅仅是 Anthropic、OpenAI 和谷歌”进行合作。 截至截止日期，这三个人工智能实验室已向政府提供了框架草案的反馈。

人工智能公司渴望尽快获得明确的指导，以确定他们正在开发的模型是否可能受到该框架的约束。 据知情人士透露，白宫计划于当地时间周二与相关企业举行幕僚级会议，审查该框架。 当世界上最强大的AI模型将面临什么样的监管规则时，即使是提供反馈的公司也仍蒙在鼓里，而这个“完成但不可见”的框架本身可能已经揭示了很多。
